title: Researching Bitcoin Products
description: Turn craft into judgment: audit a real product with a shared rubric, talk to real users under a strict ethics kit, and publish the findings. Governs Gate 3.

objectives: Run a heuristic evaluation with the shared 12-criterion rubric — no screenshot, no score
Interview Bitcoin users as a privacy-sensitive population: stories over opinions, silence as a tool
Apply the five research ethics rules, the consent script, and anonymization at the source
Run a lightweight moderated usability test (3–5 participants) and map observations to rubric criteria

resources.title: NN/g — "10 Usability Heuristics for User Interface Design"
resources.desc: CORE. You met these in Lesson 3 as a designer; reread them now as an evaluator. Group A of our rubric is built directly on them.

resources.title: NN/g — "How to Conduct a Heuristic Evaluation"
resources.desc: CORE. The method itself: evaluator process, severity ratings, how findings get written. Our audit adapts this; knowing the original makes you faster.

resources.title: Erika Hall — "Just Enough Research" (2024 Mule Books edition)
resources.desc: CORE BOOK. The pragmatic method reference for this whole phase. Priority chapters: Interviewing (for your Gate 3 interviews) and Evaluative Research. Short, funny, ruthless about bad research.

resources.title: Bitcoin Design Guide — Case Studies
resources.desc: CORE. Worked examples of real product analysis by working Bitcoin designers: the WalletScrutiny redesign (note its five user interviews), Blixt Wallet onboarding, and the Payjoin experience study. Study structure and tone; this is the publishing standard you're stepping into.

resources.title: Bitcoin Design Community — Design Review recordings
resources.desc: VIDEO. Watch one recent review specifically for findings language: how working designers phrase a problem, cite a principle, and propose a fix without attacking the maker. Your audit's tone check in video form. Facilitator posts the current pick in #week-6.

assignment.title: GATE 3: Published UX audit
assignment.submissionFormat: Published audit + annotated Figma appendix (checkpoint: product + research plan in Week 6)
